content.title: December 10, 1954: Dr. John Stapp - Testing Pioneer
December 10, 1954: Dr. John Stapp - Testing Pioneer
The Human Rocket Ride: The Story Behind John Stapp's Ultimate Speed Test
60 years later: still the fastest man on earth

results:
The search confirms the headline figure: Stapp's December 10, 1954 run on the Sonic Wind I sled hit about 632 mph, and sources agree on that number.

- **Speed:** The Air Force Flight Test Center says Stapp reached 632 mph within five seconds at Holloman AFB, New Mexico (Lieutenant Colonel John Paul Stapp, M.D., reached a speed of 632mph within five seconds on the high-speed rocket sled test track at Holloman AFB, NM.). A metric conversion appears in another source, which gives 1,017 km/h.
- **G-forces differ by source:** Acceleration figures vary between about 19 and 20.6 Gs. The Air Force puts acceleration at 19 Gs and deceleration at 40 Gs (19 G acceleration and 40 Gs deceleration). The New Mexico Space Museum gives 46.2 Gs for the stop, which took 1.4 seconds.
- **Context:** Holloman's own history page says the run was the last human test at the Test Track. The experiment was meant to find at what speed a pilot could safely eject.

content.text:
**答案：632 英里/小时**（约 1,017 公里/小时）

1954 年 12 月 10 日，Stapp 在新墨西哥州霍洛曼空军基地坐 Sonic Wind I 号火箭滑车，大约 5 秒内加速到 632 英里/小时。这个数在各个来源里都一样。几个来源给的 G 值对不上，不过这里只问速度，没有影响。

只搜了 1 次。

- [December 10, 1954: Dr. John Stapp - Testing Pioneer（美国空军试飞中心）](https://www.aftc.af.mil/News/On-This-Day-in-Test-History/Article-Display-Test-History/Article/2411198/december-10-1954-dr-john-stapp-testing-pioneer/)
